items.title: Retirement: Pod name dimension in AKS pod platform metrics
items.description:
Beginning September 30, 2027, support for the pod name dimension on the following Azure Monitor platform metrics is retiring, and these metrics are transitioning to aggregate pod counters:
  • Number of pods by phase (kube_pod_status_phase)
  • Number of pods in Ready state (kube_pod_status_ready)
After this change:
  • Metric names remain unchanged.
  • Aggregate pod counts remain available.
  • Namespace-level monitoring scenarios remain supported.
  • The pod name dimension will no longer be available for filtering, grouping, or alerting.
During the deprecation period, AKS will maintain both the existing and the new aggregate implementations. Both are populated with data, existing monitoring experiences will continue to function, and you will have at least one year of historical data in the aggregate implementation before retirement.
You may be affected if any dashboard, workbook, alert, automation, or monitoring workflow:
  • Uses kube_pod_status_phase or kube_pod_status_ready and filters on the pod name dimension.
  • Splits or groups results by the pod name dimension.
Recommended action:
  • If you use aggregate pod counts, no action is required.
  • If you use the pod name dimension, update dashboards, alerts, workbooks, and automation before September 30, 2027. For pod-level monitoring and troubleshooting, we recommend using Azure Monitor Managed Prometheus and Kubernetes-native pod metrics.
Help and support
If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A.

items.title: Retirement: Azure App Service on Azure Stack Hub
items.description:
Azure App Service on Azure Stack Hub will be retired on September 30, 2029. 

Starting September 30, 2026, new installations will no longer be supported, and no new product releases, features, or enhancements will be made available. Existing supported deployments can continue to run and upgrade to the latest available release until retirement. 

Customers should begin planning migration to Azure App Service in Azure now to continue receiving support, security updates, platform improvements, and new capabilities. 

On September 30th, 2029, App Service on Azure Stack will reach retirement and Microsoft support will end. 

Recommended action  

Assessand migrate applications as soon as possible. Azure App Service in Azure provides a fully managed platform with global availability, Windows and Linux hosting options, autoscale, deployment slots, advanced networking and security, Azure services integration, and continuous innovation. 

For applications with complex Windows dependencies, evaluate Managed Instance on Azure App Service. It can help accelerate migration for applications requiring registry access, COM components, custom runtimes, or other Windows-specific dependencies. 

For a successful transition, inventory applications and dependencies, assess compatibility, select the appropriate Azure hosting target, migrate code, configuration, and data, validate workloads, and complete migration before September 30, 2029. 

Learn more:  

  • Benefits 
  • Plan 
  • Migrate

items.title: Retirement: Support for Java 8, 11 and 17 will end on September 1, 2027
items.description:
On September 1, 2027 support for Java 8, 11 and 17 will end. Your apps that are hosted on App Service will continue to run, but security updates will no longer be available, and we’ll no longer provide customer service for Java 8, 11 and 17.

Required action  

To avoid potential security vulnerabilities and minimize risk for your App Service apps, follow the steps to upgrade your app to Java 25 before September 1, 2027. 

Learn more.

items.title: Retirement: Always Encrypted with Intel SGX Enclaves
items.description:
Always Encrypted with Intel SGX enclaves in Azure SQL Database will retire on October 31, 2027 as support for SGX-enabled DC-series hardware is phased out. Customers should transition to Virtualization-Based Security (VBS) enclaves, a hardware-independent alternative, or consider SQL Server on Confidential VMs.

Customer impact

After retirement, workloads using Intel SGX enclaves will no longer have enclave functionality. Databases running on DC-series compute tiers should be migrated to supported compute tiers to continue using enclave-enabled features.

Recommended actions

  • Migrate from DC-series to a supported Standard-series (non-DC) compute tier.
  • Enable VBS enclaves for Always Encrypted. No attestation is required.
  • Update client drivers to versions that support VBS enclaves.
  • Update connection strings to remove SGX attestation parameters and use VBS enclave mode.
We recommend planning and validating your migration well in advance of the retirement date to ensure a smooth transition.

items.title: Public Preview: AKS on bare metal now on Ubuntu
items.description:
Running Kubernetes on-premises often means adding a virtualization layer, adapting to unfamiliar infrastructure, or giving up control over the hardware and software your applications depend on. For AI workloads, these tradeoffs can limit access to local data, reduce available compute capacity, and restrict your choice of GPUs, drivers, and runtimes.

AKS on bare metal Ubuntu, now in public preview, brings the AKS experience directly to customer owned Ubuntu infrastructure. Deploy a complete Kubernetes cluster on your hardware using Azure CLI. Choose the CPU and GPU hardware and supporting software stack that fit your workloads.

Run applications close to your data, dedicate more infrastructure capacity to your workloads, and manage Kubernetes through familiar AKS and Azure workflows. You keep the flexibility of Ubuntu and your hardware while extending a consistent AKS operating model to your on-premises environment.

Learn more.
